gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-nag-mundari: Tightly knit rows of text mark Oswald as strong, packed display type. Noto Sans Nag Mundari, a sans-serif, brings the snap: half-unwrapped c shapes and small letters that rival the caps.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-nand: Marker-fat titles, hollow in every curve: Red Hat Display looks bold. And Noto Sans Nandinagari, a sans, holds a stretch of copy with generous openings and short ascenders.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-ogha: Clean wide gaps in the e sit under a marker heading from Red Hat Display. Noto Sans Ogham, a sans, walks running copy on high-bodied small letters that look dark and solid.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Solid-block words and tails held back from the body make Noto Sans Ol Chiki read clean under Chubbo. Chubbo does the marker shout; Noto Sans Ol Chiki does the unswollen running line.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-old-: A constant-width marker line marks Red Hat Display as bold display. Noto Sans Old Italic, a sans-serif, shares the sheet, with almost no cap step and curve endings kept well apart.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-old-north-ara: A dense, high-bodied lowercase band with tongs-open terminals makes the body read approachable. Noto Sans Old North Arabian, a sans, holds that band, while Oswald wants a few large packed words.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-old-: Contemporary open counters sit under Red Hat Display's single-weight outline, a lofty lowercase filling the line. Noto Sans Old Persian, a plain sans, still reads a size down.
gen-fs-rx-100-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Crowded, futuristic letters with a dominant x-height and no modulation: RX100 hits in a brief burst. Be Vietnam Pro, a sans-serif, and that heading share one steel-rod sheet.
gen-fs-segment-fs-merriweather-sans: Segment spaces neighboring letters wide, a stocky midzone with breathing counters. Merriweather Sans, a plain sans, still reads a size down, while those titles want only a few spaced lines.
gen-fs-segment-fs-nunito: Big round lowercase bowls and terminals that stop short of the stem make Nunito read approachable under Segment. Nunito, a plain sans, prefers copy that stays brief and round.
gen-fs-stardom-montserrat: Dramatic thick diagonals with hairline counter-strokes mark Stardom as bold display. And Montserrat, a sans-serif, glides like wire through running copy, while the heading prefers a compact burst of words.
gen-fs-tanker-fs-fira-sans: Tanker crowds heavy, commanding letters with inward-turning curves and tiny gaps. Fira Sans, a plain sans, does the open s and unshaded line, while Tanker owns a compact burst of titles.
gen-fs-zina-outfit: Broad-nib fat downstrokes against threadlike upstrokes: Zina looks refined and striking. Outfit, a sans-serif, holds a stretch of copy on cable-bent curves, while those titles want a quick glance.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-instrument-sans: Stencil-cut channels of one weight, no pinched curves: Balsamiq Sans looks bold and expressive. Instrument Sans, a plain sans, brings the snap: pincer-open c against that stencil channel.
gen-gf-bellota-rubik: Distinctive far-flung s ends, every stroke one stylus wide, mark Bellota as commanding display. Rubik, a plain sans, still holds if the body is made large, with big small letters and open rounds.
